_fidelity_note: Item-level enumeration for chest_pain/exertional_breathlessness_or_fatigue/palpitations/syncope+murmur/fever_with_joint_pains reproduces the source decision table exactly (possibility counts and modules-opened columns all match). Discriminators not given verbatim in the source (thyrotoxicosis, reflux, anaemia, TB pericarditis, pleuritis/pneumonitis, pericarditis) are Vitalis-authored, clinically reasonable, not literally sourced. The irregular_pulse and diaphoresis symptom->item mappings are Vitalis inferences (the source table gives no row for either) rather than transcribed rows. discriminator_question rephrases each discriminator as a single bedside-checkable yes/no question the doctor can answer immediately (history/exam only) -- deliberately not investigation-dependent, since the differential review happens before ECG/vitals are collected in this flow; ACS and pulmonary embolism's questions are narrowed to their bedside-checkable component only, the ECG/troponin component is confirmed by the ST-elevation hard exit and Angina's own Gate 0 immediately afterward, not by this screen.

symptoms.label: Irregularly irregular pulse noted on exam

items.label: Aortic dissection
items.exclusion_policy_reason: Tier 1 -- a negative examination finding makes this unlikely, not impossible. Requires one deliberate confirmation before it leaves the list.

items.label: Acute coronary syndrome
items.discriminator: Rest pain, dynamic ECG changes, troponin rise
items.discriminator_question: Pain at rest, or unrelieved by rest?
items.exclusion_policy_reason: Never excluded here -- ACS is owned formally by the angina module's Gate 0.

items.label: Pulmonary embolism
items.discriminator: Pleuritic pain with hypoxia, no ECG explanation
items.exclusion_policy_reason: Tier 1 -- a negative examination finding makes this unlikely, not impossible. Requires one deliberate confirmation before it leaves the list.

items.label: Pneumothorax

items.discriminator_question: Sudden onset with reduced breath sounds on one side?
items.exclusion_policy_reason: Tier 1 -- a negative examination finding makes this unlikely, not impossible. Requires one deliberate confirmation before it leaves the list.

items.label: Severe aortic stenosis

items.exclusion_policy_reason: Tier 1 -- a negative examination finding makes this unlikely, not impossible. Requires one deliberate confirmation before it leaves the list.

items.discriminator_question: Exertional, relieved by rest or nitrate within minutes?

items.exclusion_policy_reason: Absence of its discriminator on examination is sufficient to rule this out.

items.exclusion_policy_reason: Absence of its discriminator on examination is sufficient to rule this out.

items.exclusion_policy_reason: Absence of its discriminator on examination is sufficient to rule this out.

_symptom_item_map_source: plan/mock consult.md -- the checkbox -> possibilities table. Every row here traces to that document; do not widen a row without updating it there first.

findings.question: Are the peripheral pulses equal in both arms?
findings.help: Radial pulses, both sides. Add the femorals if you can.

findings.question: Is the pain worse on breathing in?
findings.help: Pleuritic or positional pain. One answer settles four possibilities at once.

findings.question: Weight loss, night sweats, or fever lasting more than a week?
findings.help: The question that surfaces TB pericarditis, which a standard cardiac differential misses.

findings.question: Is the pain reproduced by pressing on the chest wall, or by moving the neck or arm?
Brought on by exertion, and gone within minutes of resting?
findings.help: 'No' here also means the pain occurs at rest or is unrelieved by it, which is what keeps ACS on the list.

findings.question: Fever with joint pains, or migratory joint pain after a sore throat?
Conjunctival or palmar pallor?
findings.help: Optional. Pallor puts anaemia higher up the list; its absence does not take anaemia off, because only a haemogram can.

findings.question: Related to meals or lying flat, and relieved by antacids?
findings.help: Optional. Can only move reflux up the list; clearing it needs a treatment trial or endoscopy.

_findings_source: Consolidated question set. private/context/vitalis-exclusion-engine.md: one shared finding resolves several differential items, so the doctor records ~5 observations instead of answering one question per possibility. Items whose exclusion_policy is 'never' hang off a promotes_only finding (or share one with another item) -- no examination finding can clear them, so asking is optional and their absence never removes them.
